source: NASA/JPL Small-Body Database, CNEOS fireball and close-approach APIs

bodies.km: ផ្កាយដុះកន្ទុយហាលី
bodies.info: The most famous comet: back every 75–76 years (last 1986, next 2061). Its dust gives the Eta Aquariid and Orionid meteor showers.

bodies.km: ផ្កាយដុះកន្ទុយអេនកេ
bodies.info: The shortest-period bright comet: around the Sun every 3.3 years. Parent of the Taurid meteors.

bodies.km: ផ្កាយដុះកន្ទុយស្វីហ្វ-ធើថល
bodies.info: A 26 km comet that returns every 133 years (next 2126). Earth crosses its dust every August: the Perseids.

bodies.km: ផ្កាយដុះកន្ទុយធែមផល-ធើថល
bodies.info: Returns every 33 years. Its dust trail gives the Leonid meteors in November, sometimes a meteor storm.

bodies.km: ផ្កាយដុះកន្ទុយហ្សាកូប៊ីនី-ហ្ស៊ីនណឺ
bodies.info: A small comet every 6.6 years; parent of the October Draconids.

bodies.km: ផ្កាយដុះកន្ទុយផុន-ប្រ៊ុក
bodies.info: The "devil comet" with horn-like outbursts, back every 71 years (seen 2024).

bodies.km: ផ្កាយដុះកន្ទុយ ស៊ូជីនសាន-អាត្លាស
bodies.info: A bright comet seen from Cambodia in October 2024. It comes from the far Oort cloud and takes about 80,000 years to return, or may never come back.

bodies.km: 3I/ATLAS វត្ថុមកពីក្រៅប្រព័ន្ធព្រះអាទិត្យ
bodies.info: Only the third object known to come from another star system (found July 2025). Its path is open (hyperbolic): it passes once and leaves the Solar System for ever.
The largest object in the asteroid belt (940 km), now called a dwarf planet. Visited by NASA Dawn.
The third-largest asteroid (510 km), on a steeply tilted orbit.
The brightest asteroid (525 km), with a huge crater at its south pole. Many meteorites found on Earth (HED meteorites) came from Vesta.
The fourth-largest asteroid (410 km), nearly round.
A 17 km near-Earth asteroid, the first one a spacecraft landed on (NEAR Shoemaker, 2001).
A 490 m near-Earth asteroid. NASA OSIRIS-REx brought a sample back to Earth in 2023.

bodies.km: អាប៉ូហ្វីស
bodies.info: A 340 m asteroid that will pass only 32,000 km from Earth on 13 April 2029, closer than geostationary satellites. No impact risk.
A rocky asteroid that comes very close to the Sun; its dust makes the Geminid meteor shower in December.
A 900 m carbon-rich asteroid; Japan’s Hayabusa2 brought samples home in 2020.

bodies.km: អ៊ីតូកាវ៉ា
bodies.info: A small peanut-shaped asteroid (330 m); Hayabusa brought the first asteroid sample to Earth in 2010.
A 780 m asteroid with a small moon, Dimorphos. In 2022 NASA DART crashed into Dimorphos and changed its orbit: the first test of planetary defence.
